correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge2\), averaging reduces only the objective value to two weights. Exact invariant spectrum is [1,1-(2m+1)a,1-a-2mb,(1-a-mb) with multiplicity 2m-2]. For s=1-a and y=mb, max(|s-y|,|s-2y|)>=s/3, equality iff y=2s/3; hub row capacity a<=\(1/(2m)\) yields sharp mu>0. The proposed weights attain the bound since |1-(2m+1)a|=\(1/(2m)\)<=mu for \(m\ge2\). For any optimal P, Q=mu I-P+J is PSD; averaging Q gives Q(P*) which has nullspace containing both peripheral zero-sum spaces. As the average consists of PSD forms, each original Q annihilates those spaces. This forces every hub-edge vector to be classwise constant, every cross-edge row and column equal, and all peripheral diagonals equal to mu, hence P is automorphism invariant and equal to P*. The proof covers all n=\(m\ge2\) and all feasible real symmetric stochastic matrices. SymPy exact spectra for \(m=2\)..9 and 1331 full-matrix numerical checks reproduced it; samples are not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The prior all-k-partite spectral reduction (Boyd et al., 2007/2009, section 5.3.2) already supplies the matrices for the invariant SDP and is expressly credited. The distinguishing assertion is that its singleton-cone balanced-biclique optimum is unique among the much larger class of all potentially asymmetric-under-automorphisms kernels. The source shows orbit reductions, not an all-optimizers rigidity theorem; the new nullspace/equality argument is necessary. The 2010 equal-sized pseudo-distance-regular multipartite class and 2020 clique-lifted class are different. Searches of literature and published mathematical claims found no implication of the global uniqueness result, although unindexed equivalence remains a risk.

value.rationale: The graph is the natural balanced bipartite communication architecture augmented by a universal hub. Generic convexity guarantees that a symmetrized optimum exists but says nothing about possible asymmetric alternative allocations. Full global uniqueness is a genuine network-design structural invariant: every hub edge must carry \(1/(2m)\), every crossing edge must carry \((2m-1)/(3m^2)\), all are essential and the hub must have no holding. The exact improvement over optimally weighted K_{m,m} is \(1/(6m)\), quantifying the benefit of the hub. This all-optimizers statement, rather than a simple substitution into the prior SDP block formula, supplies the value.
